blocks.text:
No. `pir` (this featherweight pi-compatible Rust agent) does **not** do context compaction. Its `--help` shows no `--compact`/compaction/context-summary option, and the only token-related control is `--budget`, which *stops* the turn once a cumulative in+out token cap is exceeded — it doesn't summarize or compact history to keep going.

So compared to full `pi` (which typically has auto-compaction of the transcript), `pir` here has no compaction feature: long sessions will grow the context until the budget cap halts the run (or the model's context window limits it). If you need it to handle very long sessions, the available lever is `--budget <tokens>` (a hard stop, not a compress).
